strings.game.title: GalForge — Extensions Demo
strings.char.guide.name: Guide
strings.ending.cleared.title: Orientation Complete
strings.s01.guide.welcome: Welcome to the GalForge extensions demo. I'm your guide for the next minute.
strings.s01.guide.layout: See the Layout control at the top? This game ships its own — “Visor HUD” — imported with galforge-import-layout. Switch to it any time: it re-skins this very screen, no player fork.
strings.s01.guide.adhoc: What comes next isn't ordinary dialogue — it's an adhoc scene: a little quiz the command grammar can't express, run by a developer module that galforge-import-adhoc wired into the flow.
strings.s01.guide.start: Three quick questions. Answer two correctly to pass. Ready when you are.
strings.s01.guide.pass: Nicely done — you passed. The quiz wrote your score back into the story, and we branched on the result to land here.
strings.s01.guide.fail: Close! You didn't quite pass this time — but the result still wrote back, and we branched here instead. Same machinery, different path.
strings.s01.guide.outro: That's the whole trick: a custom layout re-skins the screen, an adhoc scene adds a beat the grammar can't, and both stay lint-clean. Now go build something.
strings.quiz.title: Orientation Quiz
strings.quiz.label: Question
strings.quiz.q1: How many character sprites can the GalForge stage show at once?
strings.quiz.q1.c: As many as the scene declares.
strings.quiz.q2: When an adhoc scene finishes, what rejoins the common flow?
strings.quiz.q2.a: A brand-new scene file it writes to disk.
strings.quiz.q2.b: A result: a declared exit plus variables written back.
strings.quiz.q3: How does the runtime activate a custom stage layout?
strings.quiz.q3.a: You edit and rebuild the player's source.
strings.quiz.q3.b: It opens the layout as a separate HTML page.
strings.quiz.q3.c: It sets a data-layout attribute on the stage root.
